item.text: I’m checking a small set of primary 2024 sources for whether Biden’s rhetoric became actual governing machinery: budgets, agency launches, appointments, and enforcement. After that I’ll stop searching and synthesize the strongest claim-level items.

item.text:
**Bottom Line**  
Yes, mostly. In 2024 Biden translated a clear governing agenda into budgets, named institutions, rulemaking, and enforcement. The main counterevidence is not absence of planning, but campaign-targeted framing, one flagship plan getting blocked, and late-year coherence loss after the debate collapse.

**Accepted Claims**
- **FACT SHEET: The President's Budget Lowers Costs for the American People** | Publisher: The American Presidency Project | Date: March 11, 2024 | URL: [page](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/fact-sheet-the-presidents-budget-lowers-costs-for-the-american-people) | Claim: The budget turns Biden’s “middle out and bottom up” program into concrete spending and tax priorities for prescription drugs, health care, housing, homeownership, energy costs, and fiscal offsets. | QIDs: `8B.2`, `8B.1`
- **Biden-Harris Administration Announces First-Ever Consortium Dedicated to AI Safety** | Publisher: NIST | Date: February 8, 2024 | URL: [page](https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2024/02/biden-harris-administration-announces-first-ever-consortium-dedicated-ai) | Claim: Biden’s AI executive order became an actual institution, with a 200+ stakeholder consortium tied to red-teaming, evaluations, risk management, and watermarking. | QIDs: `8B.2`, `8B.1`
- **U.S. Secretary of Commerce Gina Raimondo Releases Strategic Vision on AI Safety, Announces Plan for Global Cooperation Among AI Safety Institutes** | Publisher: NIST | Date: May 21, 2024 | URL: [page](https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2024/05/us-secretary-commerce-gina-raimondo-releases-strategic-vision-ai-safety) | Claim: The administration set out named AI-safety goals and a global network of AI Safety Institutes, showing timeline and institution building rather than vague aspiration. | QIDs: `8B.2`
- **Biden-Harris Administration Announces Preliminary Terms with Microchip Technology to Strengthen Supply Chain Resilience for America’s Automotive, Defense, and Aerospace Industries** | Publisher: U.S. Department of Commerce | Date: January 4, 2024 | URL: [page](https://www.commerce.gov/news/press-releases/2024/01/biden-harris-administration-announces-chips-preliminary-terms-microchip) | Claim: CHIPS became a specific funding program with dollar amounts, plant expansions, job targets, and a due-diligence pipeline; 2024 Intel and Micron awards reinforce that this was a standing implementation machine, not a one-off slogan. | QIDs: `8B.2`, `8B.1`
- **Justice Department Finds Civil Rights Violations in Phoenix Police Department and City of Phoenix** | Publisher: U.S. Department of Justice | Date: June 13, 2024 | URL: [page](https://www.justice.gov/archives/opa/pr/justice-department-finds-civil-rights-violations-phoenix-police-department-and-city-phoenix) | Claim: DOJ used formal investigations and findings of unconstitutional conduct as an enforcement mechanism, showing Biden-era goals being translated into action against a subordinate institution. | QIDs: `8B.2`
- **FACT SHEET: The President’s Budget Improves Customer Experience to Better Serve the American People** | Publisher: The American Presidency Project | Date: March 11, 2024 | URL: [page](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/fact-sheet-the-presidents-budget-improves-customer-experience-better-serve-the-american) | Claim: The budget funds service-delivery modernization, including online passport renewal and expert civil servants, so the governing program is being embedded in administrative capacity. | QIDs: `8B.2`

**Counterevidence**
- **Biden has canceled $138 billion in student loans. Some say it’s not enough.** | Publisher: The Washington Post | Date: March 6, 2024 | URL: [page](https://www.washingtonpost.com/education/2024/03/06/biden-student-loan-forgiveness/) | Claim: The article says Biden was gearing up for reelection and trying to raise the profile of debt relief, which makes part of the agenda look election-targeted rather than purely programmatic. | QIDs: `8B.2`, `8B.1`
- **Federal judge temporarily blocks Biden’s student loan forgiveness plan** | Publisher: The Washington Post | Date: September 5, 2024 | URL: [page](https://www.washingtonpost.com/education/2024/09/05/federal-court-blocks-biden-student-loan-forgiveness-plan/) | Claim: A court injunction stopped a major 2024 student-debt initiative, showing that at least one flagship plan did not cleanly translate into durable, enforceable implementation. | QIDs: `8B.2`
- **Biden drops out of 2024 race after disastrous debate** | Publisher: Associated Press | Date: July 21, 2024 | URL: [page](https://www.ap.org/news-highlights/elections/2024/biden-drops-out-of-2024-race-after-disastrous-debate-inflamed-age-concerns-vp-harris-gets-his-nod/) | Claim: The debate collapse shattered confidence and forced Democrats to rebuild coherence around Harris, which weakened continuity for any second-term governing program. | QIDs: `8B.2`, `8B.1`

**Search Gap**
- I did not find strong 2024 evidence that Biden lacked a governing program or that he was pursuing a distinct regime-control blueprint. The negative evidence is mostly about campaign framing, execution limits, and late-year coherence loss, not about absence of plans, budgets, institutions, or enforcement.
